mscnews_items.@IT001: MALARIA ON THE REBOUND IN THE SOUTHEAST U.S. The Center for Disease Control in Atlanta reports that rising year-round temperatures in the Southeast have led to the return of endemic malaria and other parasites in much of the Deep South.  The invasion of the Asian "tiger mosquito" is partly blamed for the spread of both malaria and encephalitis, as it remains completely resistant to all eradication and control efforts. Travelers have been advised to stay out of New Orleans and Miami indefinitely, unless absolutely necessary. ...On Wall Street, a leading stock analyst recommended investments in several major pharmaceutical companies that are seeking approval of drugs for treatment of mala- ria and encephalitis, while drug industry representatives pooh-poohed the scurrilous rumors on The Street that the companies had anything to do with introducing such patho- gens in the Southeast.... Meanwhile, in other news from Atlanta, a major biotech firm disclosed today that one of its new genetically altered plant species, which is a cross between the prolific and fast-growing kudzu plant, a Venus flytrap, and the giant sequoia tree, has escaped from an ex- perimental farm outside Atlanta and has rapidly spread throughout much of northern Georgia in only 2 weeks. The firm advises people in the area not to get within 30 feet of the large carnivorous plants, warning that they "...can be somewhat dangerous to anything smaller than a bull elephant...."
mscnews_items.@IT002: FLORIDA SLIPPING BENEATH THE WAVES AFTER HURRICANE HITS West Palm Beach is under a foot of water today, in the wake of yesterday's hurricane that breached the dikes that protect this Florida city from the Atlantic Ocean. Like much of Florida, West Palm Beach has been pro- tected from flooding in recent years by a vastly expen- sive and ever-expanding system of dikes and sea walls, all designed to keep out the rising ocean waters.  But sea levels have risen several feet in the last two years, as a result of the rapid melting of the Ross Ice Shelf in Antarctica, and the sea finally overwhelmed the city's defenses yesterday, with the help of Hurricane Zoe, the 26th hurricane to hit Florida this season. Government climatologists describe the increased number of hurricanes and rising sea levels as "normal fluctuations in weather cycles," not caused by any alleged "greenhouse effect." Meanwhile, in Washington, auto company officials warned the House Commerce Committee that the economy would be harmed if the government re-established fuel efficiency requirements for autos, which were repealed in recent years. With unemployment approaching 20%, and Detroit's "Big 2" auto firms threatening to move all of their re- maining U.S. production offshore, Washington insiders say it is unlikely that Congress will attempt to crack down on "gas-guzzlers" again....

mscnews_items.@IT004: DEATH COUNT RISES TO 150,000 IN MEXICO CITY AS DEADLY TEMPERATURE INVERSION CONTINUES Mexico City has long been a city where migrating birds fell dead out of the sky and must be swept off the streets, as a result of almost unimaginable levels of air pollution. But over the last three days, lethal air pollution that has built up as a result of a "blocking high" pressure system centered over the Mexican metropolis has finally begun to kill off the city's human population as well, in equally vast numbers. Deaths are estimated by the Mexican government to be roughly 150,000 thus far, with no relief from the mass asphyxiations in sight.  Foreign reporters in Mexico report a nightmare scene, where the dead lie uncollected in the streets, from sidewalk to sidewalk, and where the only people able to escape the city are those few with electric- powered vehicles. No one else is able to start their cars, because there is insufficient ambient oxygen in the stag- nant air basin to operate internal combustion engines, or to even light a match. The authorities have told citizens that there is no cause for alarm, insisting that conditions will return to "nor- mal" as soon as the weather changes. A government spokesman has vehemently denied that the city's lax enforcement of air pollution laws has had anything to do with the growing catastrophe, and described the crisis as "...a temporary thing, quite manageable, just part of the price we must occasionally pay for economic progress and for our quest to become a First World industrial nation...." ....Meanwhile, in a related story, General Motors, which recently built the world's largest automobile assembly plant in Mexico City after closing its last remaining U.S. plant, announced that this year, for the first time ever, it sold more automobiles in that city than in the entire U.S market....
mscnews_items.@IT005: ISLANDS SINK, AS DEBATE OVER GREENHOUSE EFFECT CONTINUES The Maldive Islands, once a virtual paradise in the Indian Ocean, have officially ceased to exist, according to French geologists. The last residents evacuated the Maldives over a year ago, as rising sea levels (caused by the alleged "greenhouse effect," according to some environmental groups) gradually inundated the once-beautiful island group.  Most of the islands in the chain were no more than 3 feet above sea level before the rise, with the highest point only 6 feet above sea level, so that the Maldives are the first major group of islands to disappear beneath the waves, due to the rising oceans. Most of the islands are now above sea level only at low tides. In Washington, an Energy Department public relations spec- ialist reiterated the current administration's position that the rising sea levels are a result of unusually high rainfall on the Indian subcontinent and that there is "no credible scientific evidence" to support the view that the increasing use of carbon-based fuels is causing, or ever will cause, a greenhouse effect. A spokesman for the U.S. Department of Commerce stated at a news conference that U.S. investments in the Maldives were minimal, and that the disappearance of the small is- land nation will have little, if any, effect on U.S. eco- nomic interests. ....Meanwhile, in related business news, a spokesman for the American Petroleum Institute says that the future has never looked brighter for the energy industry, since the opening of the Alaska Wildlife Reserve to oil drilling and for strip mining of coal. Referring to the recent warm winters and almost tropical summers in Alaska, he noted that "...Even Mother Nature herself seems to be aiding our exploration and development activities in Alaska...."
mscnews_items.@IT006: FOOD RIOTS CONTINUE IN RUSSIA AND UKRAINE The chaotic situation in the former Soviet Union and Eastern Europe has grown more tense as food riots erupted yesterday in much of the Russian and Ukrainian republics. The entire fabric of civilization in Eastern Europe and Asian Russia seems to be breaking down, in the wake of the deadly viral epidemics resulting from use of biological weapons in last month's border war between Russia and the Ukraine. The brief but lethal Five-Day War erupted after the Ukraine refused to take necessary steps to deal with the latest meltdown of its Chernobyl reactors, which have been spewing out vast radioactive clouds for nearly 3 months, carried by prevailing winds over much of European Russia and Scandinavia. (The conflict was mercifully short, as both sides expended their entire stockpiles of chemical and biological wea- pons on each other in less than one week.) Today, hundreds of thousands of Russian citizens are re- ported to be on the march, on foot, crossing into Poland and Finland in a frantic search for food, and to escape the raging epidemics of lethal, untreatable viruses.... Meanwhile, in Washington, a Senate select committee will begin hearings tomorrow to investigate several U.S. drug and biotech companies, which allegedly were handsomely paid to help develop some of the more virulent disease strains that were used by the Ukrainian side in the war....
mscnews_items.@IT007: SLAVERY MAKING A COMEBACK IN MUCH OF THE WORLD The Anti-Slavery Society, an organization based in London that has been seeking to eradicate slavery since 1837, has finally closed its doors.  In a final press release, the Society said that its mission had failed, and that after more than a century and a half of fighting the vicious institution of slavery, it conceded that slavery is now far more prevalent than at any other time in recorded history.  The final straws, according to the press release, were the repeal of the U.S. Constitution's Thirteenth Amendment, held to be "unconstitutional" and an "impediment to interstate commerce" by Chief Justice David Duke in a 5-4 decision of the Supreme Court, a decision which was followed quickly by the passage in the U.S. Congress of a bill repealing the personal bankruptcy laws and replacing them with a law authorizing indentured servitude. The new law, pushed through Congress by banks and other lending institutions, with the active support of President Buchanan, permits creditors to impose up to twenty years of indentured servitude upon debtors who are unable to pay their bills--most of whom could have simply filed for bank- ruptcy in the past.  According to the Anti-Slavery Society, the effect of these new laws will be to create a vast new underclass of indentured servants in America.  Indentured servitude is an ancient, non-racially discriminatory ver- sion of slavery, popular in colonial America, that has already made a big comeback in Asian countries in recent decades.... Several major U.S. personnel agencies were said to already be looking into ways to take advantage of the new "free labor market" (pro-slavery) legislation, and in Chicago, one of the principal commodity exchanges is rumored to be readying new futures contracts for indentured services, now that former prohibitions on buying and selling the rights to forced labor have been effectively removed from the U.S. constitution by an activist Supreme Court....
mscnews_items.@IT008: VIOLENCE FLARES AGAIN AS CROWDS MOB U.S.-MEXICAN BORDER A San Diego, California TV station today aired videotape of Mexican border troops firing automatic weapons at point-blank range into a crowd of U.S. citizens, huddled adjacent to the recently erected barriers along the U.S.- Mexican border south of San Diego. The steel barriers, which now stretch from Brownsville, Texas to the Pacific Coast, were erected by the MEXICAN government, in order to keep out the growing hordes of jobless, homeless Americans who have desperately been seeking employment in, and entry into, Mexico in recent months. Over 4 million such U.S. "drybacks" had flooded into Mexico before the last portions of the barrier were put in place a month ago. The number of U.S. citizens killed or wounded by the border guards in this latest incident has not yet been determined, but is believed to be at least 1,000. Faced with this videotaped evidence, a spokesman for President Pelosi has at last admitted that there may be some basis for recent allegations by the American Legion and the ACLU of contin- uing atrocities being committed against American citizens by Mexican border forces. In response, the U.S. state Department has sent a strongly worded diplomatic note to Mexico City, urging that its troops exercise greater restraint, and that they refrain from using automatic weapons to disperse crowds of U.S. citizens, except when absolutely necessary to maintain order.... In a related business story, U.S. Steel, which supplied much of the steel plate for the border barriers to the Mexican government, reports that nearly all of the steel was made by its gigantic new steel mill in Monterrey, Mexico....
mscnews_items.@IT009: EPA WARNS PUBLIC TO PROTECT AGAINST SUN'S STRONGER RAYS An official of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) today warned all U.S. citizens living in northerly lati- tudes to exercise extreme care when going out of doors. Residents of all areas north of Orlando, Florida are ad- vised to wear long-sleeved garments, a hat (preferably a pith helmet) and U-V protective goggles before venturing outdoors.  In areas north of Columbia, South Carolina, it is strongly suggested that foil-lined clothing be worn, when possible, due to the intense U-V radiation, according to EPA spokesperson Mendacio Calderon.  Calderon attrib- uted the lethal levels of solar radiation to the "...normal sunspot cycle...." and he discounted any possibility that the ozone layer is disappearing.  Calderon, a former chief of public relations for a major chemical company, also in- sisted that there is no cause for alarm, and emphasized that anyone who follows the EPA's recommended precautions should have no concerns about going outdoors, for periods of up to fifteen minutes a day. When asked how animals in the wild will protect themselves, since they don't generally wear pith helmets or foil-lined clothing, Calderon said he had no further comments, and declared the press conference adjourned. ...Meanwhile, in a related business story, Reynolds Metals reports record sales of its aluminum foil products. Accor- ding to the company, large orders from a new source, the apparel industry, are fueling a banner year for the crink- ly stuff....
mscnews_items.@IT010: BANKING INDUSTRY ROLLS OUT NEW HIGH-TECH TELLER MACHINES Major U.S. banks have introduced a sophisticated new auto- matic teller machine, called the "Grabber," which is de- signed to virtually eliminate ATM theft and fraud losses. The new machines have built-in manacles, into which the user is required to place his or her wrists (or ankles), before undergoing fingerprint I.D. and DNA analysis, while punching in transactions into the ATM. A bank official explained that, "If your bank card is invalid or overdrawn, or if you punch in the wrong P.I.N. code number three times in succession, the manacles don't unlock, and a siren sounds until the security people or police arrive." (Which may be the next morning, in some cases, since it is virtually impossible to escape from the titanium alloy manacles, once they lock in. However, some miscreants, like muskrats caught in a trap, have been known to gnaw off a limb and escape before the gendarmes finally arrived, leaving only an arm or a leg behind as a grisly calling card.) Bank officials describe the new ATMs as "...extremely effective....the ultimate answer to ATM thefts and over- drafts, and bad news for deadbeats...." In an address to the American Bankers Association conven- tion in Putingrad (formerly Moscow), Russia, one enthus- iastic speaker hinted that banks are quietly working with international law enforcement agencies, including the FSB and INTERPOL, on further technical enhancements that will enable the ATMs to instantly compare a user's fingerprints and DNA with FBI and other fingerprint and DNA databases, in order to "grab" anyone wanted by any government. Targeted individuals would range from escaped serial killers to polit- ical dissidents, to individuals with overdue library cards or unpaid parking fines, any of whom would be captured instantly by the machines if they were foolish enough to use an ATM outfitted with the new "Grabber" technology....
mscnews_items.@IT011: NO MORE FREE SHOPPING AT MAJOR DEPARTMENT STORE CHAINS Several major department stores have now announced that, effective after the end of@YEAR, they will begin charging $20 admission to persons wishing to shop in their stores. A Wal-Mart spokesperson explained the new policy as being "...a natural evolution of recent trends in retailing.  It costs us a great deal of money to keep our stores open and ready for business.  So why should we let people who want to come in and browse or shop do so for free -- any more than a movie theater lets its customers in for free, or a gas station lets people use its restrooms for nothing? Charging our customers to come in and shop is all a simple matter of economics -- We can, so we will...."
mscnews_items.@IT012: CANADA'S PARLIAMENT PASSES ALIEN EXPULSION ACT BY 3-TO-1 VOTE In Ottawa, the Canadian Parliament has approved a measure designed to deal with the growing number of boat people who have been entering the country, either legally or illegal- ly, many of whom are only moderately wealthy. After years of being overwhelmed by the influx of foreign immigrants, Canada has finally reacted by electing to power the new Anglo-French Alliance Party, whose first order of business in Parliament was to adopt the strict new law, which calls for the sterilization and/or expulsion of all aliens who are unable to demonstrate a personal net worth of at least 5 billion Northern Pesos (Canadian dollars). This is the approximate equivalent of 100,000 Yen, or 1.5 million New American Dollars. The Expulsion Act appears to be targeted at U.S. and Latin American immigrants, as it will affect only a small per- centage of recent immigrants from Hong Kong and Mainland China, known locally as the "yacht people." In the U.S., the National Association of Manufacturers applaud- ed the Canadian government's action, noting that the new influx of refugees into the States should augment the U.S.'s already vast pool of cheap, unemployed, highly-skilled labor.... On a less positive note, Secretary Jimmy Swaggart of the U.S. Department of Religion and Culture said the U.S. would not accept any of the refugees who were forced to leave Canada, and suggested they go to Iran or North Korea....
mscnews_items.@IT013: FBI REPORTS THAT CAR-JACKING IS NOW THE SECOND MOST COMMON CRIME IN AMERICA Official FBI crime statistics for@YEAR indicate that car- jacking, a crime where armed toughs drag motorists out of their cars, often at gunpoint or knifepoint, before taking their cars, has reached epidemic proportions.  It now is one of the most common crimes reported in the U.S., second only to random sniper shootings.  And there is said to be an increasing overlap between these two crimes recently in urban areas, now that street gangs regularly spray any Mercedes automobile they spot with automatic weapons fire, often just to take the hood ornament as a trophy. An FBI spokesperson told CNN today that "...In a few years, we expect that all free-roaming Mercedes automobiles will be bereft of hood ornaments... for the same reason that all living rhinos in Africa now have their horns surgical- ly removed by gamekeepers... just as the only surviving giraffes in the wild are now without tails -- since their tails are highly prized as whisk brooms, they would quite naturally be killed off by poachers if the gamekeepers didn't cut off their tails first... Same principle here...." In related business news, Daimler-Chrysler, the large German auto maker and defense manufacturer, reported a 72% drop in sales of its Mercedes automobiles into the U.S. for the latest three-month period, and is reportedly considering either abandoning the U.S. market altogether, or creating an American version of its automobiles that has no hood ornament or other distinguishing insignia.... Crime has become THE big business in America, along with the construction and operation of prisons, and provision of security services.
mscnews_items.@IT014: DRUG RIOTS CONTINUE IN PORTIONS OF SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA Riots raged again last night in the Los Angeles area, where the once-posh shopping areas of Beverly Hills were largely looted and burned to the ground by enraged mobs of black and white "crackheads."  A police helicopter crewman surveying the scene from the air said the count- less number of fires looked like "...a thousand points of light."  Once again, federal troops and shelling by Navy warships have been used to quell this latest violent out- break of anarchy and random murder. Republican President Sean Hannity has declared all of Beverly Hills and much of Santa Monica federal disaster areas, and once more he pointed out that the spate of gang wars and drug riots that have broken out in@YEAR, more or less spontaneously, in all parts of the U.S. and in much of Western Europe are merely a consequence of the failure of this year's coca crop in Colombia. Congress, in special session, is considering emergency agricultural aid to Colombia's devastated coca farmers until the flow of "ghetto sedatives" resumes. ....In related business news, several major U.S. agri- business and tobacco firms have offered to help develop a reliable domestic supply of opiates and coca, if only Congress will enact the necessary enabling legislation....
mscnews_items.@IT015: WORLD POPULATION PASSES 8 BILLION MARK U.N. officials reported today that the world's human population passed the 8 billion mark in the year@TEXTSTRING, several years ahead of schedule. In a related story, the Humpback whale has been declared extinct.  A Japanese whaling ship reports having bagged the last 5 known remaining humpback whales, during a recent "research" voyage. The voyage proved to be immensely profitable, as frantic Tokyo bidders paid up to $500 per pound for the precious whale meat, a greatly prized delicacy in Japan -- particularly since this will be the last of it ever to come from Humpbacks.  Japan's whalers will next focus their research efforts on the endangered gray whale, which is down to less than 250 specimens at latest count. Meat from marine mammals has become increasingly hard to find in Tokyo seafood markets, at any price, due to intense competition from Norwegian and Icelandic whalers and the fact that dolphins, killer whales, walruses, and most whale species are now as extinct as the woolly mammoth or the elephant. Meanwhile, U.S. food companies, jealous of the exorbitant Japanese profits from whaling, are mounting a major lobby- ing effort to get Congress to approve whaling by American vessels. Several large food companies, sensing an oppor- tunity, are reported to have already acquired and fitted out whaling vessels, indicating their confidence that Congress can be persuaded (with adequate campaign largess) to rescind the U.S. ban.
mscnews_items.@IT016: OZONE HOLES CONTINUE TO WIDEN The UN Environmental Czar reported today that most of South Africa, southern Australia and the lower halves of Chile and Argentina, now known as the "Zona de los muertos," have been rendered devoid of most living organisms.  The intense solar radiation has sterilized nearly all living things on those southern continental areas and in the Antarctic Ocean. The last of millions of cattle and sheep in the affected areas died over a year ago, and the only surviving creatures south of the 35th parallel appear to be humans, most of whom are now blind or suffering from hideous cancerous growths. Stock prices plunged to near zero on the Buenos Aires bolsa, on news that the "Zona de los Muertos" or "dead zone" is now within 100 miles of that city. ...In a related development, major Western chemical compan- ies continue to argue vehemently that the HCFCs they pro- duce are not a major threat to the ozone layer, and that the entire matter of the alleged "ozone holes" needs to be studied further.  On a similar note, Russia's U.N. ambassa- dor told the Security Council today that Russia does not concede that there IS an ozone problem, and that, if there is, it is a problem of the rich Western countries, and, that, in any case, Russia intends to continue to increase its production of HCFCs and CFCs. Meanwhile, Canadian scientists confirm that Hudson Bay has become a dead sea, scorched by the ultraviolet rays pour- ing in through the north polar ozone hole....Several major hospital supply companies have previously announced that they are studying the feasibility of setting up facilities on Hudson Bay, and to begin tapping this nearly endless supply of sterilized saline solution for medical uses....
mscnews_items.@IT017: RADIATION CLOUDS DUE OVER U.S. BY END OF WEEK Huge clouds of radioactive dust from last week's nuclear clash between Libya and Syria are being carried away from Asia and Africa by the prevailing westerlies, and should reach the U.S. mainland by the end of the week. All U.S. residents are advised to store as much food and water as possible before the radioactive cloud arrives, as it may be difficult to obtain uncontaminated food or water for several years, even if you are willing to venture above ground, out of your fallout shelter. Reports are still sketchy as to who "won" the Libyan-Syrian nuclear battle, as all contact with both nations has been lost since the brief, 6-hour war. Pentagon officials stated today that they knew for some time that both parties had acquired considerable amounts of weapons-grade plutonium on the black market during the early days after the breakup of the Soviet union in 1992, plus a sophisticated delivery capability, in the form of advanced missiles purchased from India and North Korea. Apparently the outbreak of the conflict was a result of a serious miscalculation by the Syrians. They launched first, believing that the Libyans, with whom they have been quarreling for several years, lacked a nuclear capa- bility, but were on the verge of acquiring it shortly. Judging by the 60 or more nuclear blasts in Syria, and several more errant Libyan missiles that fell into nearby Jordan and Turkey, the Libyans were far better armed than the Syrians, who apparently fired only 10 nuclear missiles into Libyan population centers. At the Pentagon in Washington, a spokesperson for the U.S. Military Junta explained that the black market price of nu- clear weapons is still quite high, and that Syria lacked the oil earnings to become a major player, unlike Libya, Iran, Iraq, Indonesia, Kuwait, Algeria and other new mem- bers of the Nuclear Club. Meanwhile, armored columns from the Sudan, which reportedly has recently acquired at least one crude nuclear device, rolled into neighboring Ethiopia today, apparently seeking to capture the large U.N. food stocks in that country, where U.N. relief agencies have been trying to avert widespread famine.... In Tel Aviv, Israeli military officials expressed their gratitude to the American defense firms who illegally sold the Libyans the highly precise guidance systems that enabled the Libyans to fire 60-odd missiles into Syria without a sin- gle missile falling short into Israel.  Any such misfire, had it happened, would doubtless have touched off another, far more serious and more widespread, nuclear conflict.... Several U.S. defense suppliers expressed regret at the loss of two major customers for their guidance systems and nuclear technology, but avowedly were confident that new orders from North Korea, Myanmar (Burma), and the Iranian- financed Hezbollah group in Lebanon would more than offset any slack in their export business....
mscnews_items.@IT018: AIR NO LONGER FREE IN L.A. -- Los Angeles has become the first American city to charge for air. Since breathable air has become such a rare commodity in the Los Angeles Basin, the County Council recently approved a plan whereby the city has begun importing bottled air from Alaska, which the city is now dispensing at a number of service stations along major freeway routes. Drivers wearing oxy- gen masks, which have become quite fashionable in Southern California, can now pull into almost any gasoline station, tank up their car, and buy an hour's supply of breathable air for only fourteen dollars. Many of L.A.'s 40 million residents seem very enthusiastic about the new program. Phoenix, Denver, New York, and a number of other cities are already studying the feasibili- ty of following the lead of Los Angeles.  As always, the world's largest city, L.A., is on the cutting edge, and officials of the city's Air Resources Board are already looking several years ahead, to a time when the air in Los Angeles will be lethal to anyone with exposed skin, at which time Angelenos may be required to wear spacesuits or similar protective clothing, as wealthier residents al- ready do on most days in Third World cities like Bangkok, Sao Paulo, Miami and Shanghai, and as they formerly did in Mexico City before its collapse and abandonment.... In related news, Chevron announced approval of its plans to build a large new oil refinery in a burned-out area of Santa Monica. No one has chosen to rebuild in large areas of the L.A. Basin, particularly in Santa Monica, in the wake of the last riot and conflagration. Thus, Chevron says it was able to acquire the land for its refinery at a very reasonable price. While the refinery will be a ma- jor source of air and water pollution, there was little opposition to its construction, since no one currently lives within several miles of the chosen site, in any di- rection, in the burned-out ghost town of Santa Monica....
mscnews_items.@IT019: U.N. ISSUES HEALTH ADVISORY -- The United Nations Health Organization has released an urgent health advisory, strongly urging all people of the world to avoid swimming in ocean waters and banning the eating of fish or plant products from the oceans. The U.N. agency warns that the radioactivity level of sea water in all of the world's oceans makes it extremely hazardous for anyone to come in contact with sea water or to consume any kind of seafood. In recent years, ever-increasing leakage of radioactive wastes into rivers around the world, along with the corro- sion and breakup of nuclear reactors dumped at sea over the last 40 years by the Soviet and Western navies, have resulted in this massive radioactive contamination of the oceans. The U.N.H.O. indicated that this health advisory is expec- ted to remain in effect for at least 250,000 years.... President Kanye West, in an address to the nation from the Oval Room of the White House, told Americans that the radioactive contamination of the oceans was exactly as pro- phesied in the Old Testament, a punishment and warning of future plagues to come for America. In Tokyo, the new Japanese prime minister assured viewers of his first press conference that the dangerous radiation level in the world's oceans "...has absolutely nothing to do with the Fukushima reactors..." that were destroyed by a massive tsunami and earthquake in 2011 and which some dissidents say have been leaking vast amounts of radiation into the Pacific ever since then. Meanwhile, in Tokyo and Chicago, commodity futures on fro- zen seafood products soared to record price levels, as alert traders realized that the existing stocks of frozen fish and whale meat could not be replaced in the foreseeable future, in light of the U.N. ban.....

The new law will require anyone who boards a city bus or other Phoenix public transit to first urinate into a small metal cylinder before being allowed to board. A sophisticated new machine, called the "Instant Adjudica- tor," will then perform on-the-spot tests for some 173 different controlled substances that might be found in the urine of illicit drug users. The ever-present Secret Drug Police, who now ride on every City transit vehicle, are authorized under existing drug laws to immediately terminate anyone who fails, or refuses to take, these new mandatory drug tests. Life is cheap in this crowded desert city of 12 million souls. Under Phoenix's previously enacted "Zero Tolerance" drug law, persons found to be in possession of even minute amounts of illegal substances, or who fail a drug test, are subject to capital punishment, without benefit of trial, legal counsel, or other traditional, but costly and time-consuming protections of the Anglo-Saxon crimin- al justice system. So far, over 27,000 offenders have been liquidated in Phoenix since the new Zero Tolerance laws went into effect, 10 months ago. The extension of mandatory drug testing to all users of the city's public transit system is expected to dramatically increase the number of miscreants to be sanctioned and permanently removed from the voter rolls in coming years. mscnews_items.@IT034: UNIVERSITY OF ALABAMA FOOTBALL TEAM'S RECORD WIN STREAK ENDED, AT LONG LAST, BY NOTRE DAME, 24-23 All good things must end. mscnews_items.@IT035: CRUDE OIL PRICES TUMBLE, AS NEW PIPELINES FROM THE PERSIAN GULF OPEN, REDUCING THE IRANIAN THREAT TO GLOBAL OIL SUPPLIES The oil ministers of Saudi Arabia and Abu Dhabi announced today that major new pipelines have been completed from Saudi Arabia's oilfields to the Red Sea and from Abu Dhabi to the port of Fujairah on the Indian Ocean, both bypassing the oil shipping lanes through the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow strait in the Persian Gulf that Iran has frequently threatened to close. The new pipelines will significantly reduce Tehran's power to influence global oil markets by limiting its ability to block oil exports from the Persian Gulf. As tensions have grown between Iran and the U.S. and its European allies, the Iranian mullahs have on numerous occasions threatened to close the strait. Closing off the Strait of Hormuz, until now, would have pinched off much of the world's oil supply, which must pass through that narrow bottleneck in the Persian Gulf. At some places, the shipping lanes through the strait are only two miles wide, making it possible to cut off all shipping traffic in and out of the Gulf by simply laying a few mines, if Iran had chosen to do so. In London, the spot crude price for Brent fell sharply in active trading, as much of the "fear premium" in crude prices has been eliminated by these new and more secure routes for exporting most of the oil from the Persian Gulf region.
mscnews_items.@IT036: INTERNET CHATTER POINTS TO ANOTHER POSSIBLE MAJOR VIRUS EPIDEMIC IN WUHAN, CHINA -- CHINESE GOVERNMENT DENIES, SAYS ONLY A FEW CASES IDENTIFIED Unofficial reports leaking out of China suggest that another dangerous virus epidemic is raging in and around the city of Wuhan, coincidentally where the devastating COVID-19 virus originated back in 2019, which did major damage to the entire global economy, as a result of quarantining billions of healthy members of society. Google, YouTube and FaceBook have begun censoring any fake news that suggests the lab may have been the source of the infections. Any such claims would be in disagreement with the official position of the World Health Organization, which has stated that the lab has a perfect safety record. mscnews_items.@IT041: COLD FUSION BREAKTHROUGH AT MIT: FOSSIL FUELS TO GO THE WAY OF THE DINOSAURS? mscnews_items.@IT042: ROBOTS TAKING OVER INDUSTRY: HUMAN WORKERS BECOMING SUPERFLUOUS Robotics has become the world's largest single industry, as numerous companies, almost fully automated and using robots to build robots, continue to produce robots, large and small. The robots now serve almost every conceivable function, from piloting jetliners to nanorobots performing gene therapy at a molecular level. Like previous industrial revolutions, however, this one is not without casualties, as robots continue to replace human workers throughout every industry, from cab drivers and construction workers, to heart surgeons and lawyers. mscnews_items.@IT045: DEFLATION AND RECESSION FEARS GROW, AS COMMODITY PRICES CONTINUE TO PLUNGE Gold prices on London and NyMex exchanges fell sharply today, for the first time since the 2011 collapse, as central banks in Europe and Australia continue to dump the rapidly depreciating precious metal, in the wake of the continuing subprime mortgage loan crisis, which has undermined confidence in the safety of banks and other financial institutions throughout the world. mscnews_items.@IT046: RAMPANT INFLATION PROMPTS FED CRACKDOWN ON INTEREST RATES Expressing concerns that monetary policy has been too loose in recent years, U.S. Federal Reserve Board Chair @TEXTSTRING said that the time has come to rein in an "irrationally exuberant" economy (to use the terminology of a former Fed Chairman), by raising interest rates "to the sky, if necessary." mscnews_items.@IT047: BIOTECH REVOLUTION IS TURNING INTO A GLOBAL CRISIS, AS GENETICALLY-MODIFIED DNA SPREADS FAR BEYOND THE LABORATORY The U.N. Food and Agricultural Organization has issued a warning that the world may be facing widespread famines and severe human health problems and environmental damage, as a consequence of science's creation of genetically-modified ("GM") species of plants. Biotech firms that developed GM plants are being blamed for releasing the modified DNA strains into the global environment. According to U.N. experts, scientists inserting animal genes in food plants, or inserting genes that make non-food plants like cotton or hemp highly toxic to insects and other predators, were very shortsighted in failing to realize that pollen from fields of GM crops would blow into the wild and cross-pollinate with wild plants, as well as contaminating the DNA of other, non-GM crops. As a result of a peanut gene sequence being used in GM cotton plants to strengthen cotton's resistance to molds and fungi, the gene sequence surprised scientists by migrating into grain crops, such as wheat and rice, making those common foods inedible to a significant minority of the population, who go into shock or die if they consume even trace amounts of peanuts or any part of the peanut plant, including the grain crops that have now been contaminated with the peanut gene. Similarly, genes that make various plants toxic to insects have now found their way into much of the major food crops grown throughout the world, making the food harvested from such crops highly toxic to humans and livestock. From one end of the world to the other, governments and farmers are scrambling to build greenhouses, with filtered air to keep out pollen from genetically engineered plants outside, since it is rapidly becoming impossible to raise edible food crops outside a closely-controlled environment, such as a hermetically sealed greenhouse. Many Third World countries have been affected less severely so far, as the GM genes were not widely introduced in such countries before the problems became apparent, but Third World countries will eventually be in serious trouble as winds carry the GM plants' pollen to every corner of the planet, unless they can find the capital to replace outdoor agriculture with green- houses. mscnews_items.@IT056: FLOOD OF ASIAN, MEXICAN IMPORTS INTO U.S. MARKET TRIGGERS CALLS FOR PROTECTIONISM BY U.S. LAWMAKERS, INDUSTRY AND LABOR A massive rally was held on the steps of the U.S. capitol today, by unemployed workers and others demanding that the U.S. restrict imports of foreign-made goods, as the U.S. continues to be flooded by imports of low-priced goods from China, Korea, Vietnam, Japan and Mexico. mscnews_items.@IT057: U.S. CONGRESS ENACTS TRADE TARIFFS, DESPITE PRESIDENTIAL VETO Both houses of the U.S. Congress have overwhelmingly passed new legislation, the "Alien Goods Exclusion Act," that will impose tariffs on imports from most of America's main trading partners, including China, Japan, Korea, Mexico, Chile, much of Europe, and Canada. mscnews_items.@IT058: VIRTUAL TRADE WAR HAS ERUPTED BETWEEN U.S., ASIA, AND EUROPE International tensions have grown, stretching good relations almost to the breaking point, following the U.S. withdrawal from and repudiation of the GATT and NAFTA agreements, and the enactment by the U.S. Congress of heavy tariffs on most kinds of imported goods. mscnews_items.@IT059: INVESTORS CELEBRATE, AS TRADE WAR ENDS Jubilant investors bid up the prices of stocks and bonds on all major global bourses today, celebrating the early end to what had the potential of becoming a major trade war between the major Asian, European, Latin American and U.S. trading blocs. mscnews_items.@IT060: TRADE WAR CONTINUES TO ESCALATE; SMUGGLING GROWS TO BE A BIG BUSINESS, AS THE WORLD ECONOMY CONTINUES IN A TAILSPIN No end seems in sight to the steady escalation of trade tensions between all the world's major trading blocs. They were soon followed by walkouts by equally angry trade delegates from the U.K., Japan, Germany, and more and more other nations, so that after three hours had passed, the only remaining trade envoys in the large Geneva conference hall were the representatives from Belize, Ethiopia, and Nepal, who, after brief deliberations, decided to disband the trade talks and go home. The trade war that has erupted is causing a wide range of economic dislocations in nearly every country. One of the less savory side effects of the trade war is the return of high levels of smuggling, with even large and supposedly reputable corporations and shipping companies engaging in smuggling activities, in an effort to somehow get embargoed goods into countries that have banned most kinds of non- essential imports of food, textiles, building materials and most types of consumer and capital goods. The trade crisis was exemplified recently by the sinking of a British freighter by Korean gunboats, several kilo- meters off the coast of South Korea, as a Korean coastal patrol vessel caught the Brits redhanded, in the act of smuggling cola drinks into Korea, by anchoring offshore in the darkness and shuttling in cases of soft drinks in small, fast "cigarette boats," to their waiting accomplices on the shore. The South Korean government has recently announced a "zero tolerance" policy regarding illegal imports, and the torpedoing and sinking of a British vessel has now signaled to the world that the South Koreans' "get tough" policy is not to be taken lightly. In London, Whitehall has requested an explanation from the South Korean government, but Britain is not expected to do much more than lodge a formal protest, in light of the U.K.'s own sinking of a Chilean smuggling ship off the coast of Scotland last week, which regrettably was sent to the bottom with all hands lost, after a fierce bombing attack by Royal Air Force fighter-bombers....
mscnews_items.@IT061: INFLATION SPIRALLING OUT OF CONTROL, AS GLOBAL TRADE GRINDS TO A HALT, AND ECONOMIES STAGNATE Economies from Alaska to New Zealand, from Tadzhikistan to Peru, continue to falter, as the global trade war quietly sputters away to a low-level conflict. Unfortunately, the surpluses were all spent on various other social programs over the years, and the Trust Fund merely consisted of hundreds of billions of "IOU's" to the govern- ment, from itself, all stored in large warehouses near Washington, D.C.. Now that all the trillions of surpluses have all been spent on re-electing the incumbent politicians, and it has become evident to everyone that the "Trust Fund" consists of nothing but worthless IOU's, the realization has at last set in that the U.S. government is nearing financial, as well as moral, bankruptcy, and will only be able to pay its Social Security pension obligations by printing vast quantities of increasingly worthless money, a process euphemistically referred to as "quantitative easing." Even the few who were able to save for retirement are now seeing those savings evaporate, as inflation erodes the value of the U.S. dollar and most other national currencies. Hard times seem here to stay, as the U.S. dollar is now comparable in buying power to the Turkish Lira or the Colombian Peso. The U.S. seems headed down the same road as the nation of Zimbabwe, where inflation rates reached trillions of percent per day as the once thriving country sank in an abyss of inflation and poverty, for all but the Marxist ruling class.
mscnews_items.@IT062: CHINESE FINALLY COMPLETE REUNIFICATION China marked the reunification of Taiwan with Mainland China today by large scale celebrations, fireworks and military parades, as the Communist government in Beijing finally com- pleted the revolution that began shortly after World War II, and which, with regard to Taiwan, had been stalled ever since the Nationalist Chinese under Chiang Kai-Shek had fled there from Mao some @TEXTSTRING years earlier. mscnews_items.@IT063: CONFLUENCE OF TECHNOLOGICAL TRENDS PROMISES NEW ERA OF PLENTY Economists and investment analysts are increasingly coming to believe that the world is on the verge of a "new era of plenty" as a result of several technological trends which are coming together.
